title: For Fun
text: I’ve been playing ultimate frisbee since my freshman year of college, and it has become one of my favorite parts of my time at CWRU. Over the years, I’ve grown into the role of a handler, where I get to help lead offensive plays, distribute the disc, and create opportunities for my teammates. I love the combination of strategy, athleticism, and teamwork that makes ultimate so much fun.

text:
Knitting

This “jasper jumper” I made was one of my first knitting projects! It includes a unique pattern of knitting and purling around the sweater to create this beautiful pattern. This took me several months to make. As a beginner I am very proud of myself!

title: For Fun
text:
Oil Pastels











I started experimenting with oil pastels over the summer because I wanted to find more creative activities I could enjoy outside. I’ve always liked making things and exploring different ways to be creative, so oil pastels quickly became a fun new hobby. My girlfriend actually came up with the idea of having me draw potatoes as a way to challenge myself. They might seem like simple subjects, but getting their rounded shapes, shadows, textures, and subtle color differences to look realistic is surprisingly difficult! What started as a little challenge has become a fun way to practice, experiment, and push myself creatively.

Hey there! My name is Enysah Roberts. I’m originally from Pitsburgh, PA (Go Steelers!) and I’m currently a senior at Case Western Reserve University studying Biochemistry with a minor in Religious Studies. I’m currently involved in biomedical research at the Cleveland Clinic, where I get to explore the molecular mechanisms underlying invasive lobular breast cancer and exploring better treatment options for this understudied subtype. For more information on this research, click my “Research” tab! My interests grew out of my love for chemistry and the chemical interactions that occur at a molecular level and therefore influence cellular behavior. Understanding the mechanisms at this cellular level can inform us researchers how to develop more effective, targeted treatments for patients. As a researcher, I’m especially interested in understanding how diseases develop and finding new ways to approach conditions that remain difficult to treat.
After graduation in May 2027, I hope to continue building my research experience as a research assistant at Case. I’m particularly interested in joining a pharmacology lab, where I can gain more experience in drug discovery and broaden my understanding of how potential therapies are developed and evaluated. I’m excited to explore research beyond my current focus in cancer biology.
Outside of academics and research, I play ultimate frisbee, which has become one of my favorite ways to challenge myself, stay active, and spend time with my teammates. When I’m looking for more slower pace activities, I enjoy drawing with oil pastels, knitting, and finding new creative projects to work on. I also love working out simply because I enjoy moving and trying new things. Whether I’m in the lab, on the field, or working on something creative, I like having opportunities to learn, challenge myself, and make things along the way. For more information, click my “For Fun” tab!
